title: First of Two
goal: The result borrows only from text. Write the signature so label's short lifetime does not matter.
hints: result outlives label. If label shares 'a, the returned borrow shrinks to label's short life - E0597.
The return only ever borrows from text. Give label its own lifetime and the constraint disappears.
explanation: With one shared 'a, the compiler must pick a lifetime that fits BOTH inputs at the call site - and the block-scoped label drags 'a down to its own short life, killing `result` before its println (E0597). The return value never touches label, so the honest signature gives label a separate 'b: now the result is tied to text alone and lives happily past the block. Rule of thumb: only inputs the output actually borrows from should share its lifetime.
